## Purpose

This procedure describes a rapid method for measuring the potential rate
of ammonium oxidation in soils using a shaken soil slurry. The method
provides an estimate of the activity of the existing ammonium-oxidizing
microbial population at the time of sampling. It is based on ISO 15685
(*Soil quality -- Determination of potential nitrification and
inhibition of nitrification -- Rapid test by ammonium oxidation*)
[@iso15685].

Ammonium oxidation is the first step in autotrophic nitrification.
Soil is incubated in a buffered (pH 7.2) ammonium sulfate solution
with sodium chlorate added to inhibit nitrite oxidation. The
accumulation of nitrite (NO~2~^-^) over a 6-hour incubation period
serves as the measure of potential nitrification activity. Because the
generation time of ammonia-oxidizing bacteria exceeds 10 hours, the
assay measures the activity of the population present at sampling, not
population growth.

This method can be used to compare soils (e.g., polluted vs. reference),
to screen the effects of management practices or chemical substances on
nitrifying communities, and to evaluate the impact of biosolids or waste
materials on soil nitrification.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Field-moist soils containing a population of
  nitrifying microorganisms; assessment of nitrification inhibition by
  chemical substances (except volatiles with Henry's constant H > 1),
  biosolid extracts, and polluted soil mixtures
- **Does not apply to:** Soils with no detectable nitrifying population;
  measurement of in situ nitrification rates (this is a potential
  activity assay under optimized conditions); volatile inhibitors
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve experimental design, ensure training compliance |
| Lab Manager       | Prepare reagents, maintain shaking incubator |
| Trained Personnel | Perform assay, record and report results    |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Sodium chlorate (NaClO~3~) is an oxidizer; avoid
  contact with organic materials and combustible substances. Potassium
  chloride (4 M KCl) is a mild irritant. Ammonium sulfate is a mild
  irritant.
- **Physical:** The orbital shaking incubator has moving parts; keep
  hair and loose clothing clear. Centrifuge operation poses standard
  mechanical hazards.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves

### Emergency Procedures

For chemical spills, refer to
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).
For sodium chlorate spills, do not use organic absorbents (sawdust,
paper towels); use vermiculite or sand.

### Equipment

| Item                          | Notes                                     |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Orbital shaking incubator     | Thermostatically controlled at 25 +/- 2 C; capable of 175 rpm |
| Erlenmeyer flasks (250 mL)   | One per replicate                         |
| Centrifuge                    | Capable of 3,000 x g; see *SOP-L108* or *SOP-L109* |
| Analytical balance            | 0.001 g resolution; see [SOP-L102](SOP-L102-using-balances.qmd) |
| Volumetric flasks (100 mL, 1 L) | Class A                                |
| Graduated cylinders           | 10, 100, 1000 mL                         |
| Pipettes                      | 2 mL (for slurry sampling) and assorted   |
| Test tubes with caps          | For subsamples                            |
| Filter funnels and filter paper | High-filtration-speed paper; chemical purity can be below the highest grade |
| pH meter                      | Calibrated per [SOP-L300](SOP-L300-pH-conductivity-bench.qmd) |

### Reagents

| Reagent                       | Concentration / Preparation               |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Distilled or deionized water  | From [*SOP-L11*](SOP-L11-milli-q-water.qmd) |
| Potassium dihydrogen phosphate (KH~2~PO~4~) | 0.2 mol/L solution       |
| Dipotassium hydrogen phosphate (K~2~HPO~4~) | 0.2 mol/L solution       |
| Sodium chlorate (NaClO~3~)   | 0.5 mol/L solution                        |
| Ammonium sulfate ((NH~4~)~2~SO~4~) | Solid; 0.198 g per liter of test medium |
| Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO~3~) | 5 mmol/L solution (optional; see Section 6.2) |
| Potassium chloride (KCl)     | 4 mol/L solution (extraction/stop solution) |


## Procedure

### Stock Solution A (Phosphate Buffer)

Combine the following in a volumetric flask and bring to 200 mL with
distilled water:

- 28 mL of 0.2 mol/L KH~2~PO~4~
- 72 mL of 0.2 mol/L K~2~HPO~4~

This yields a phosphate buffer at approximately pH 7.2.

### Test Medium

Prepare 1 L of test medium as follows:

1. Transfer 10 mL of Stock Solution A to a 1 L volumetric flask
2. Add 10--30 mL of 0.5 mol/L NaClO~3~ (see note below on
   concentration selection)
3. Add 0.198 g of (NH~4~)~2~SO~4~
4. If a carbon source is needed (e.g., when testing biosolids with high
   nitrate), add 10 mL of 5 mmol/L NaHCO~3~
5. Dilute to 1 L with distilled water
6. Verify that the pH is approximately 7.2; adjust if necessary

The final test medium contains approximately 1 mmol/L potassium
phosphate buffer, 5--15 mmol/L sodium chlorate, and 1.5 mmol/L
ammonium sulfate.

::: {.callout-note}
The sodium chlorate concentration should be sufficient to inhibit
biological nitrite oxidation without negatively affecting ammonium
oxidation. If the appropriate concentration for your soil type is
unknown, run a preliminary trial at 5, 10, and 15 mmol/L NaClO~3~ to
identify the optimal level.
:::

### Preparing the 4 M KCl Stop Solution

Dissolve 298.2 g KCl in distilled water and bring to 1 L in a
volumetric flask. This solution is used to halt ammonium oxidation at
each sampling time.

### Soil Moisture Determination

Determine the gravimetric moisture content of the soil per
[SOP-L400](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd) (dry at 105 C, 24 h). This value
is needed to calculate the volume of water in the initial soil sample
and to express results on a dry-mass basis.

### Setting Up the Incubation

1. Weigh approximately 25 g of field-moist soil into each of at least
   three replicate 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks
2. Calculate the volume of water already present in the soil:

$$
V_{\text{water}} = M_{\text{soil}} \times \theta_g
$$

where $M_{\text{soil}}$ = mass of moist soil (g) and $\theta_g$ =
gravimetric moisture content (g water / g dry soil).

3. Calculate the volume of test medium to add:

$$
V_{\text{medium}} = V_{\text{total}} - V_{\text{water}}
$$

where $V_{\text{total}}$ = desired total liquid volume (typically
100 mL).

4. Add the calculated volume of test medium to each flask
5. Place the flasks upright on the orbital shaking incubator set to
   25 +/- 2 C and 175 rpm (sufficient to keep solids suspended)

::: {.callout-important}
If testing chemical substances, dissolve them in the phosphate buffer
and add to the test medium before diluting to 1 L. For substances with
low water solubility, use mechanical dispersion or a low-toxicity
vehicle (organic solvent, emulsifier). If a vehicle is used, include an
additional control to assess its effect on ammonium oxidation.
:::

### Sampling the Slurry

1. At 2 h and 6 h after the start of incubation, shake each flask well
   to resuspend solids and withdraw a 2 mL aliquot of the slurry.
   Ensure the ratio of solution to soil is consistent across all
   samples.
2. Dispense the 2 mL aliquot into a test tube
3. Immediately add 2 mL of 4 M KCl to stop ammonium oxidation
4. Centrifuge at 3,000 x g for 2 minutes, or filter through
   high-speed filter paper
5. Transfer the clear supernatant or filtrate to a clean, labeled tube

### Nitrite Analysis

Analyze the extracts for NO~2~^-^-N using a suitable colorimetric
method (e.g., ISO 14256-2; diazotization with sulfanilamide and
N-(1-naphthyl)ethylenediamine). Extracts may be stored at 4--8 C but
must be analyzed within 24 hours.


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### Calculations

**Potential ammonium oxidation rate:**

$$
\text{Rate} = \frac{[\text{NO}_2^{-}\text{-N}]_{6h} - [\text{NO}_2^{-}\text{-N}]_{2h}}{\Delta t \times M_{\text{dry}}} \times V_{\text{total}}
$$

where the NO~2~^-^-N concentrations are in ug/mL (= mg/L), $\Delta t$
= time interval (4 h), $M_{\text{dry}}$ = dry mass of soil (g), and
$V_{\text{total}}$ = total liquid volume in the flask (mL). Report
results as ng NO~2~^-^-N per g dry soil per hour.

**Inhibition (%) by a test chemical:**

$$
\text{Inhibition} \; (\%) = \frac{R_{\text{control}} - R_{\text{treatment}}}{R_{\text{control}}} \times 100
$$

where $R$ = ammonium oxidation rate.

**Toxicity assessment for polluted soil mixtures:**

When mixing polluted and unpolluted (reference) soils, the polluted
soil is considered toxic if:

$$
A_m + s_m < 0.9 \times \frac{A_c + A_p}{2}
$$

where $A_m$ = mean activity in the mixture, $s_m$ = standard deviation
in the mixture, $A_c$ = mean activity in the control soil, and $A_p$ =
mean activity in the polluted soil (each tested separately). This
threshold applies with a minimum of four replicates.

### QC Requirements

- Use a minimum of three replicates per treatment
- Four replicates are required when applying the toxicity assessment
  equation above
- Include a negative control (soil with no ammonium addition) and a
  positive control (reference soil with known nitrification activity)
  in each batch
- Verify that ammonium oxidation is linear between the 2 h and 6 h
  sampling points. If non-linearity is suspected, add sampling at 0 h
  and 4 h to characterize the time course.
- Blank controls (test medium without soil) should show no significant
  nitrite accumulation
- Report the coefficient of variation among replicates. A CV greater
  than 15% suggests sampling inconsistency or soil heterogeneity;
  consider additional replicates.


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Soil slurries (non-hazardous) | Drain liquid; dispose of soil in standard trash |
| KCl extracts                  | Drain with copious water                 |
| NaClO~3~-containing solutions | Collect in oxidizer waste; EH&S pickup. Do not mix with organic waste. |
| Used filter paper and tubes   | Standard trash (if non-hazardous soil)   |

## Training Record

Before performing the nitrification potential assay independently,
personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   and [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
   training
3. Review the SDS for sodium chlorate
4. Complete [SOP-L400 Soil Moisture](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd) training
5. Observe a trained operator perform the full assay from slurry setup
   through nitrite analysis
6. Perform the assay under supervision with acceptable replicate
   precision (CV less than 15%)
7. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Example Calculation {.appendix}

```{r}
#| label: nitrification-potential-calc
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# Nitrification potential calculation per ISO 15685

# Input data
no2_2h_mg_L <- 0.15       # NO2-N at 2 h (mg/L in the extract)
no2_6h_mg_L <- 0.95       # NO2-N at 6 h (mg/L in the extract)
delta_t_h <- 4             # Time interval (h)
soil_moist_g <- 25.0       # Mass of field-moist soil (g)
theta_g <- 0.22            # Gravimetric moisture (g water / g dry soil)
V_total_mL <- 100          # Total liquid volume in the flask (mL)

# Dry mass of soil
M_dry_g <- soil_moist_g / (1 + theta_g)

# Potential ammonium oxidation rate (ng NO2-N / g dry soil / h)
# Convert mg/L to ug/mL (same units), then multiply by V_total to get
# total ug in the flask, divide by dry mass and time, convert to ng.
rate_ng_per_g_per_h <- ((no2_6h_mg_L - no2_2h_mg_L) *
                          V_total_mL / (delta_t_h * M_dry_g)) * 1000

cat(sprintf("Dry soil mass:            %.2f g\n", M_dry_g))
cat(sprintf("Delta NO2-N:              %.2f mg/L\n",
            no2_6h_mg_L - no2_2h_mg_L))
cat(sprintf("Nitrification potential:  %.1f ng NO2-N / g dry soil / h\n",
            rate_ng_per_g_per_h))
```

## Appendix C: Troubleshooting {.appendix}

| Symptom                       | Probable Cause                  | Corrective Action              |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| No nitrite accumulation       | Soil has no active nitrifying population; NaClO~3~ concentration too high | Test a reference soil in parallel; reduce NaClO~3~ to 5 mmol/L |
| Non-linear NO~2~^-^ accumulation | Nitrifier population growing during incubation; substrate depletion | Add intermediate time points (0 h, 4 h); use only the linear portion of the curve |
| High variability among replicates | Heterogeneous soil; inconsistent slurry sampling | Sieve and mix soil thoroughly; ensure slurry is well-shaken before each aliquot |
| Nitrite detected in controls (no NH~4~^+^) | Background nitrification from soil organic N | Note in results; subtract control values from treatment values |
| NaClO~3~ appears to inhibit ammonium oxidation | Concentration too high for this soil | Run a NaClO~3~ dose-response trial (5, 10, 15 mmol/L) |
